verdict.rationale: First-party docs describe an open source version of RudderStack (a standalone data plane and control plane backed by PostgreSQL), so the product's own source is readable. The docs never name the license or link a repository, and community threads describe moves from SSPL to AGPLv3 and later to the Elastic License, leaving it unclear whether the current license is truly open. Missing for 10: an explicitly named OSI-approved license in first-party docs, a documented public source repository link, and independent confirmation of the current license terms.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can read the product's source under an open license

citations.quote: The open source version of RudderStack is a standalone system dependent only on a database (PostgreSQL)
It consists of 2 major components: data plane and control plane
explains why Rudderstack changed their license to Elastic a few weeks ago!
